mainTopic: Can one act of שחיטה for עבודה זרה break three prohibitions at once, and can a person forbid an animal that is not his?
overview: The גמרא continues testing רב הונא's ruling that cutting one סימן of an animal for עבודה זרה makes it forbidden. It tests the ruling against a ברייתא: one who slaughters a חטאת on שבת, outside the עזרה, for עבודה זרה brings three חטאות. The problem is that once the animal is forbidden, finishing the cut is like 'chopping dirt' and should not count as שחוטי חוץ. רב פפא first places the case in a bird חטאת. The גמרא objects that עולא, whom רב הונא follows, says even a tiny act forbids the animal. A second answer, that the person said he worships only at the end of the שחיטה, fails because then the ברייתא could have spoken of any קרבן. מר זוטרא in the name of רב פפא gives the final answer: a bird whose windpipe was already half cut, so one tiny cut makes all three prohibitions happen at once. רב פפא then notes that the difficulty comes from two details in רב הונא's ruling: 'one סימן' and 'his fellow's animal.' Owning a חטאת for כפרה does not make it his own. Finally, רב נחמן, רב עמרם and רב יצחק rule that a person cannot forbid what is not his, and the גמרא begins a challenge to them from the same ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the cut is like chopping dirt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that once the animal becomes forbidden through עבודה זרה, the rest of the שחיטה is meaningless, like cutting into dirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is just chopping in dirt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that one cut can make a person liable for three sins at once. Once the animal is forbidden for עבודה זרה, finishing the cut should not count as slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being liable for שחוטי חוץ requires an animal that is fit to be a קרבן. If the first part of the cut already made it forbidden through עבודה זרה, what is left is a disqualified animal. Cutting it is like cutting dirt, so there should be no liability for שחוטי חוץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Chopping in dirt: an act with no legal meaning
Slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה
Idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the animal stopped being a קרבן in category. The point is that, at the moment the cut is finished, it is already forbidden and unfit to be offered. So finishing the cut no longer counts as slaughtering a fit קרבן outside.

phrases.english: He is just chopping in dirt!
phrases.notes: Once the animal is already forbidden for idol worship, finishing the cut does nothing, like cutting into the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge from the previous amud, where the ברייתא of three חטאות was brought against רב הונא's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that once one סימן is cut for עבודה זרה the animal is forbidden. The ברייתא, which makes the slaughterer liable for three חטאות at once, contradicts it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב הונא, the animal is forbidden as soon as one סימן is cut for עבודה זרה. So the rest of the cut is done on a forbidden, unfit animal and cannot count as שחוטי חוץ. Yet the ברייתא makes him liable for all three.

steps.title: A bird חטאת: everything happens at once
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the case is a bird חטאת, where cutting one סימן is enough, so all three prohibitions happen at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here we are dealing with a bird חטאת, where all of them come together at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by setting the case in a bird חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird חטאת needs only one סימן to be cut. So the act that forbids the animal through עבודה זרה and the act that finishes the שחיטה are the same act. Nothing happens 'later' to an already-forbidden animal, so all three sins happen together.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird sin offering
Together, at the same time
We are dealing with

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Here we are dealing with a bird sin offering,
phrases.notes: For a bird חטאת, cutting just one סימן is enough.

phrases.english: where all of them come at the same time.
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the three prohibitions: שבת, slaughtering outside, and idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָכָא בְּחַטַּאת הָעוֹף עָסְקִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific situation (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each prohibition happens at a different stage of the cut, so the animal is forbidden before the שחיטה is done
steps.terutzMaskana: In a bird חטאת, one cut finishes the שחיטה, so all three prohibitions happen together

steps.title: רב הונא follows עולא, who says even a tiny act forbids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב פפא's answer. רב הונא follows עולא, and for עולא even the smallest act forbids the animal, so even one סימן is cut while the animal is already forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, whose view did רב הונא follow when he said his ruling? עולא's. And עולא says that even a tiny act makes it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's answer by pointing out which opinion רב הונא's ruling depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's ruling only works if worshipping with the animal makes it forbidden, and that is עולא's view. But עולא holds that even a tiny act is enough. So the moment the knife starts the one סימן of the bird, the animal is already forbidden, and the 'chopping in dirt' problem comes right back.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, after all (opens a line of reasoning)
According to whom?
His ruling
Any act at all, even a tiny one

phrases.english: Now, Rav Huna,
according to whom did he say his ruling?

phrases.aramaic: כְּעוּלָּא, וְעוּלָּא מַעֲשֶׂה כֹּל דְּהוּ קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: According to עולא, and עולא says even a tiny act.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי רַב הוּנָא כְּמַאן אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's answer that a bird חטאת solves the timing problem
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under עולא, even starting the one סימן forbids the animal. So the rest of the cut is still done on a forbidden animal.

steps.title: He said he is worshipping only at the end of the שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: the person stated that his worship is the completion of the שחיטה, so the animal becomes forbidden only at the end, together with the other prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where he says that he is worshipping it at the end of the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב פפא's answer and gives a different solution to the timing problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person says from the start that his act of worship is only the finishing of the שחיטה, the animal does not become forbidden in the middle. It becomes forbidden only at the final moment, which is also when the שחיטה is complete. That way all three sins happen together, even according to עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he says
The end, the completion, of the slaughter
He worships it

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he says
that he is worshipping it at the end of the slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בְּאוֹמֵר בִּגְמַר זְבִיחָה הוּא עוֹבְדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב פפא's answer after it was rejected
steps.terutzResolutionType: New case setting based on the person's stated intent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal is forbidden from the start of the cut, so finishing it is chopping dirt
steps.terutzMaskana: Because he said his worship is at the end, the animal is forbidden only at the moment the שחיטה is complete, so all three come together

steps.title: Then why speak specifically of a חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks that if the answer depends on the person's statement, the case would work with any קרבן. So why was it taught about a חטאת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why specifically a חטאת? Let it teach us about any offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty against the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב פפא's answer, the חטאת mattered, because a bird חטאת needs only one סימן. Under the new answer, the timing works for any animal, since it depends only on what the person said. So naming a חטאת seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why specifically this case?
An offering, any קרבן

phrases.english: If so, why specifically a sin offering?
Let it teach us about any offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אִירְיָא חַטָּאת? לַישְׁמְעִינַן זֶבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new answer from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he worships at the end of the שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the timing depends only on his statement, the חטאת detail adds nothing. The case should have been taught with any זבח.

steps.title: A bird with a half-cut windpipe
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, quoting רב פפא, says the ברייתא is about a bird חטאת whose windpipe was already half damaged. One tiny cut completes the שחיטה, so all the prohibitions happen at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר זוטרא said in the name of רב פפא: What case are we dealing with? A case where half of the windpipe was already damaged. The person added a tiny cut and finished the שחיטה, so all the prohibitions come together at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that explains why the ברייתא specifically spoke about a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא holds that even the smallest act of עבודה זרה forbids the animal. Here, the smallest possible cut is also the cut that completes the bird's שחיטה, because half the windpipe was already cut. So the moment the animal becomes forbidden is exactly the moment the שחיטה is done. This only works with a bird, where cutting one סימן is enough, and that explains the חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a source to a specific situation.
The windpipe, one of the two סימנים cut in שחיטה.
Damaged or already cut.
Any amount at all, even the tiniest.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rather, Mar Zutra said in the name of Rav Pappa:
phrases.notes: "Rather" means we drop the answer from Step 4 (the person's statement) and go back to the bird חטאת idea.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where half of the windpipe was already damaged,
and he added to it any tiny amount and completed it,
so that all of them come together at the same time.
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all three prohibitions in the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5's question of why the ברייתא chose a חטאת, and also solves Step 3's problem with עולא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting even one full סימן takes time, so with עולא the animal is forbidden before the שחיטה ends.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a half-cut windpipe, the tiniest cut both forbids the animal and completes the שחיטה, all at once.

steps.title: The difficulty comes from 'one סימן'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that the חטאת is a problem only because רב הונא said the animal becomes forbidden after one סימן. Otherwise we could explain that עולא's 'act' means a full, significant act.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If רב הונא had not said 'one סימן,' the חטאת would not be a difficulty for him. We could say: what is the 'act' that forbids the animal? A significant act, meaning the completed שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא looks back and points out exactly which detail in רב הונא's ruling caused the whole difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an animal became forbidden only at the end of a full act of slaughter, it would always become forbidden together with the other prohibitions, and the ברייתא would fit easily. But רב הונא said it becomes forbidden after one סימן. That shows a partial act already counts, and that is what created the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for...
A refutation, a strong challenge.
A big or significant act.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא סִימָן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: If not for the fact that Rav Huna said "one סימן,"
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא's ruling that once one סימן is cut for עבודה זרה, the animal is forbidden.

phrases.english: the חטאת would not be a refutation of him.
What is "an act"? A significant act.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא סִימָן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side comment that explains where the difficulty from Steps 1 and 3 (the חטאת ברייתא against רב הונא) really came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the 'one סימן' detail forces us to say a small act forbids the animal. Without it, 'act' could mean a completed act.

steps.title: The difficulty also comes from 'his fellow's animal'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds a second point. The חטאת is a problem only because רב הונא's ruling was about someone else's animal. Otherwise we could say a person can forbid his own animal but not someone else's, and a חטאת is not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: If רב הונא had not said 'his fellow's animal,' the חטאת would not be a difficulty for him. What is the reason? A person can make his own animal forbidden, but he cannot make his fellow's animal forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא points out a second detail in רב הונא's ruling that creates the difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person could only forbid an animal that belongs to him, a חטאת would not become forbidden at the start of the שחיטה, because it is not really his. But רב הונא ruled that even another person's animal becomes forbidden, so 'it isn't his' does not help, and the difficulty stays.

keyTerms.meaning: Another person's animal.
He is able to forbid.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בֶּהֱמַת חֲבֵרוֹ,
phrases.english: If not for the fact that Rav Huna said "the animal of his fellow,"
the חטאת would not be a refutation of him.
What is the reason?
His own animal, he is able to forbid;
his fellow's animal, he is not able to forbid.
phrases.notes: The idea is that a חטאת is holy and does not really belong to the owner, so it would be like someone else's animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בֶּהֱמַת חֲבֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel comment by רב פפא, built the same way as Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the 'fellow's animal' detail, we could say a חטאת is not forbidden early because it is not the owner's to forbid.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say this. It seems obvious that a חטאת is not the owner's own animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's second comment as unnecessary, and this sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of course a holy חטאת is not the owner's private property, so why make a point of it? The next step explains what we might have thought otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why was it necessary to say?

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's point that a חטאת counts as someone else's animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is self-evident, so there seems to be no reason to say it.

steps.title: Owning it for כפרה is not real ownership
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we might have thought a חטאת counts as the owner's own animal, since he has a stake in it for his כפרה. רב פפא teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since he owns it for the purpose of כפרה, it is like his own animal. So רב פפא teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge by showing a real mistake someone could have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner of a חטאת does have a connection to it, since it brings him כפרה. Someone might think that is enough to count as his animal, so he could forbid it. רב פפא teaches that this connection is not real ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said...
He owns it for the purpose of כפרה (atonement).
So it teaches us (that this is not so).

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is a bird חטאת with a half-cut windpipe, where one tiny cut makes all the prohibitions happen at once. The whole difficulty comes from two details in רב הונא's ruling: 'one סימן' and 'his fellow's animal.'

phrases.english: You might have said:
since he owns it for atonement,
it is like his own animal;
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא כֵּיוָן דְּקָנֵי לֵיהּ לְכַפָּרָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: showing a possible mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Owning the חטאת for כפרה makes it count as his own animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Owning it for כפרה is not enough. It is still not his to forbid.

steps.title: Three אמוראים: A person cannot forbid what is not his
steps.stepSummary: After a memory aid for their names, רב נחמן, רב עמרם and רב יצחק rule that a person cannot make forbidden an item that does not belong to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: נ-ע-צ.) רב נחמן, רב עמרם and רב יצחק say: a person cannot make forbidden something that is not his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from three אמוראים: if you do something forbidden, like עבודה זרה, with an item that is not yours, you cannot make that item forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, רב פפא only imagined the idea that a person cannot forbid someone else's animal. Now we see that three real אמוראים actually hold this view. This opens a new discussion: does the ברייתא about the חטאת agree with them?

keyTerms.term: אֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין שֶׁלּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person cannot make forbidden an item that does not belong to him
Here it means a memory aid, a short code to help remember names

steps.confusionAlert: In the earlier steps, סימן meant one of the two pipes cut in שחיטה. Here it means something else entirely: a memory aid for the names of the חכמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule decides whether one person's forbidden act, such as עבודה זרה, can make another person's property forbidden. The rest of the sugya tests it against the ברייתא.

phrases.english: (Memory aid: נ, ע, צ.)
phrases.notes: These letters help you remember the speakers: נ for נחמן, ע for עמרם, צ for יצחק.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן, וְרַב עַמְרָם, וְרַב יִצְחָק אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman, Rav Amram, and Rav Yitzḥak say:
A person does not make forbidden
an item that is not his.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן, וְרַב עַמְרָם, וְרַב יִצְחָק אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the idea רב פפא only imagined in step 8 into a real opinion held by three אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person cannot make forbidden an item that does not belong to him.

steps.title: Challenge begins from the ברייתא of the חטאת slaughtered for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the three אמוראים by bringing back the ברייתא of the חטאת slaughtered on שבת outside the מקדש for עבודה זרה. It reminds us that the ברייתא was explained as a bird חטאת with a half-damaged windpipe, so that all three prohibitions happen at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: One who slaughters a חטאת on שבת, outside the מקדש, for עבודה זרה, must bring three חטאות. And we explained that it is a bird חטאת whose windpipe was already half damaged. The reason it has to be a bird חטאת is that then all three prohibitions happen at the same moment...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against the three אמוראים. It brings back the ברייתא and the explanation from step 6, and starts to point out why the case had to be a bird. The challenge is completed on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was set as a bird חטאת so that all three prohibitions happen together. The גמרא is about to ask what this teaches about an ordinary animal, where things happen in stages. That will test whether a person can forbid a חטאת, which is not his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering a קרבן outside the מקדש, which is forbidden
And we explained it as (we set the source in a specific case)
A windpipe that is already damaged

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ברייתא from the earlier steps. The גמרא is not starting over. It brings the ברייתא back to use it against a new opinion.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who slaughters a sin offering on Shabbat
outside the Temple, for idol worship,
is liable to bring three sin offerings.
And we explained it as a bird sin offering
phrases.notes: This points back to the answer of מר זוטרא in the name of רב פפא earlier.

phrases.english: and where half the windpipe was already damaged.
The reason is that it is a bird sin offering,
since all of them come at the same moment,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the three prohibitions: שבת, slaughtering outside the מקדש, and עבודה זרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַשּׁוֹחֵט חַטָּאת בַּשַּׁבָּת בַּחוּץ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 11 by using the ברייתא and the explanation from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רב נחמן, רב עמרם and רב יצחק that a person cannot forbid an item that is not his.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא needed a bird so that everything happens at once. The גמרא is about to infer that with an ordinary animal, the עבודה זרה prohibition would make it forbidden early, even though a חטאת is not the slaughterer's own. That would contradict the three אמוראים. The inference is finished on the next amud.
